pr.body:
One potential problem we have with batch processing is that any one slow item will clog up the whole batch. This pr implements a queueing method instead, where we keep N queues that each have their own workers. There's still a chance of individual items backlogging a queue, but we can try increased concurrency here to reduce the chances of that happening

<!-- Describe your PR here. -->
pr.title: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism

raw_findings.body: The shared FixedQueuePool's worker threads are stopped and its queues are shut down; the next strategy instance still points at this dead pool, so subsequent work_queue.put() calls raise queue.ShutDown, are swallowed in submit()'s except block, and the offset is immediately marked add+complete without the message ever reaching result_processor, causing silent message loss while the offset is still committed as processed.
raw_findings.evidence:
def close(self) -> None:
        self.shutdown_event.set()
        self.commit_thread.join(timeout=5.0)
        self.queue_pool.shutdown()

    def terminate(self) -> None:
        self.shutdown_event.set()
        self.queue_pool.shutdown()
raw_findings.failure_mode: Consumer silently drops and commits messages after a rebalance instead of processing them, causing data loss without any error surfaced.
raw_findings.impact: The shared FixedQueuePool's worker threads are stopped and its queues are shut down; the next strategy instance still points at this dead pool, so subsequent work_queue.put() calls raise queue.ShutDown, are swallowed in submit()'s except block, and the offset is immediately marked add+complete without the message ever reaching result_processor, causing silent message loss while the offset is still committed as processed.
raw_findings.root_cause: Per-strategy-instance lifecycle methods tear down a resource (queue_pool) that is intentionally owned and shared at the factory level across multiple strategy instantiations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not call self.queue_pool.shutdown() from the per-instance close()/terminate(); only stop the commit_thread there, and shut down the FixedQueuePool exactly once from ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown(), consistent with how multiprocessing_pool is managed.
raw_findings.title: close()/terminate() destroy the factory-owned shared queue_pool, breaking reuse across partition rebalances
raw_findings.trigger: Arroyo invokes close() or terminate() on the SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy during a partition rebalance/revocation, then calls factory.create_with_partitions() again for the new assignment, which reuses the same factory-owned self.queue_pool object (the pool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and only nulled out in factory.shutdown(), mirroring how multiprocessing_pool persists across rebalances).

raw_findings.body: The timeout argument is discarded; close() always blocks up to its own hardcoded 5.0s commit_thread.join() plus up to 5.0s per worker join inside queue_pool.shutdown(), so shutdown duration is decoupled from the caller's requested timeout, which can cause the process supervisor to force-kill the consumer before graceful shutdown completes.
raw_findings.evidence:
def join(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
        self.close()
raw_findings.failure_mode: Violates the ProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) contract, making shutdown timing unpredictable.
raw_findings.impact: The timeout argument is discarded; close() always blocks up to its own hardcoded 5.0s commit_thread.join() plus up to 5.0s per worker join inside queue_pool.shutdown(), so shutdown duration is decoupled from the caller's requested timeout, which can cause the process supervisor to force-kill the consumer before graceful shutdown completes.
raw_findings.root_cause: join() forwards unconditionally to close() without passing along the timeout argument.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Thread the timeout parameter through to bound commit_thread.join(timeout) and the worker joins inside queue_pool.shutdown(timeout).
raw_findings.title: join(timeout) ignores the caller-provided timeout
raw_findings.trigger: Arroyo's StreamProcessor calls strategy.join(timeout) with a specific shutdown deadline (e.g. a short timeout during a fast rebalance or SIGTERM handling).

raw_findings.body: Because 0 is falsy, `max_workers or 20` silently substitutes 20 queues instead of honoring or rejecting the explicit value, masking a misconfiguration and running with an unexpected number of worker queues.
raw_findings.evidence: num_queues=max_workers or 20,  # Number of parallel queues
raw_findings.failure_mode: Misconfiguration is silently masked rather than surfaced, complicating debugging of queue-count issues.
raw_findings.impact: Because 0 is falsy, `max_workers or 20` silently substitutes 20 queues instead of honoring or rejecting the explicit value, masking a misconfiguration and running with an unexpected number of worker queues.
raw_findings.root_cause: Using the `or` operator for a default value treats the valid falsy integer 0 the same as None.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace with an explicit None check, e.g. `num_queues=max_workers if max_workers is not None else 20`.
raw_findings.title: `max_workers or 20` silently overrides an explicit max_workers=0
raw_findings.trigger: An operator explicitly passes --max-workers 0 (or any code path passes max_workers=0) intending to configure zero/minimal parallelism.

raw_findings.body: The except clause is dead code that misleadingly suggests a queue shutdown can occur mid-processing here, reducing readability and correctness of the intended shutdown handling for future maintainers.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead/misleading exception handling obscures actual control flow.
raw_findings.impact: The except clause is dead code that misleadingly suggests a queue shutdown can occur mid-processing here, reducing readability and correctness of the intended shutdown handling for future maintainers.
raw_findings.root_cause: Exception handling for the get() call was duplicated onto an unrelated code block without verifying applicability.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant `except queue.ShutDown: break` from around the processing block since it can never trigger there.
raw_findings.title: Unreachable queue.ShutDown handler around result_processor invocation
raw_findings.trigger: This except clause wraps the sentry_sdk.start_transaction()/self.result_processor(...) block, neither of which can raise queue.ShutDown (that exception only originates from Queue.get()/put(), already handled at the earlier work_queue.get() call).

raw_findings.body: Committing offsets from a thread other than the one Arroyo's StreamProcessor uses to drive poll()/submit() deviates from the expected single-threaded strategy execution model and can race with the underlying Kafka consumer client's internal state when commit and poll are invoked from different threads.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Potential thread-safety violation of the Arroyo/Kafka client commit contract, risking undefined behavior under concurrent commit and poll.
raw_findings.impact: Committing offsets from a thread other than the one Arroyo's StreamProcessor uses to drive poll()/submit() deviates from the expected single-threaded strategy execution model and can race with the underlying Kafka consumer client's internal state when commit and poll are invoked from different threads.
raw_findings.root_cause: A background thread was introduced to periodically invoke the commit callback rather than performing commits from the strategy's own synchronously-invoked methods.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Drive offset commit checks from poll() (called synchronously by StreamProcessor) instead of a separate background thread, e.g. compute and commit committable offsets inside SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll().
raw_findings.title: Offset commits are issued from a separate background thread instead of the strategy's poll()/submit() path
raw_findings.trigger: The dedicated commit_thread wakes up every second and calls self.commit_function(committable), which ultimately invokes Arroyo's Commit callable/underlying Kafka consumer commit, concurrently with the main thread calling submit()/poll() on the same strategy.

Without evidence that Arroyo/Kafka client prohibits commits from background threads, this is ungrounded speculation about potential issues.

validated_findings.impact: A regression where close()/terminate() destroys the shared queue_pool (breaking subsequent create_with_partitions calls and causing silent message loss on rebalance) would not be caught by the existing test suite.
validated_findings.root_cause: Test coverage for thread-queue-parallel mode only exercises a single create_with_partitions call followed by factory.shutdown(), never the strategy-level close()/terminate() -> re-create_with_partitions rebalance sequence.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that calls close() (or terminate()) on the strategy from create_with_partitions, then calls factory.create_with_partitions() again and asserts newly submitted messages are still processed and offsets committed.
